clue.text: Seek answer in smithy

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the word for the smithy

parts.note: a smithy is a blacksmith's forge

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a reply in a blacksmith's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to search about for food or supplies, so it means to seek.

clue.text: Hunger of celebrity eating at home

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fame is celebrity
in means at home

explanation.surface: A star who eats only at home is starving.
explanation.definitionFit: Famine is extreme scarcity of food, hence widespread hunger.

clue.text: Conservative position adopted by footballer

definitions.meaning: a winger playing on the right of the pitch

explanation.definitionFit: The term means both politically conservative and the right-hand forward position in football.

clue.text: Pound: that'll bring smile to daughter

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: A pound coin will cheer up a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money but is the verb meaning to crush.
explanation.definitionFit: To grind is to pound something into small particles.

clue.text: Abusive expression's applied to Conservative's attempt to gain sympathy

parts.note: SOB, short for son of a bitch, is a term of abuse; with the possessive 's it gives SOB'S
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political insult is hurled at a Tory who is fishing for pity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearful tale told to win pity is an idiom for any plea designed to arouse compassion.

clue.text: Sea dog, one holding Blue Riband, perhaps

definitions.meaning: read literally as a fast hound of the waves
the Blue Riband was the award for the fastest Atlantic crossing by a liner

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the nickname of a fast transatlantic liner, a contender for the Blue Riband speed record.

clue.text: Two ways to court bird

parts.note: to spoon is to kiss and cuddle, one way of courting
to bill, as in bill and coo, is another way of courting

explanation.surface: There are two methods of wooing a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is old British slang for a girlfriend, which the surface exploits; here it is the wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird named for its flat, spoon-shaped beak.

clue.text: Nothing on side of car is outstanding

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
a wing is the body panel over a car's wheel

explanation.surface: A car with no damage to its side is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Money owing is still to be paid, i.e. outstanding.

clue.text: In ancient city rising, king enters to have final victory of war …

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so one piece is placed inside
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer
K is the chess abbreviation for king
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A king marches into a rising ancient city to win the war's decisive battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns TROY into YORT, and 'enters' puts K inside it; Yorktown, 1781, ended the American War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: The siege of Yorktown was the last major battle of the American War of Independence.

clue.text: … in town that he has invaded, revolutionary leader takes little time to end war

parts.note: Bury is a town in Lancashire

indicators.note: has invaded means is placed inside, so one word goes into another

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary leader
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader conquers a town and soon brings the war to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has invaded' signals the insertion; Bury is a Lancashire town, and the surface's war hides the idiom for making peace.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to make peace, ending a quarrel or war.

clue.text: Dimensions of gun made it unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of these three words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a gun's odd make gave it its size.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnitude is size or extent, which is what dimensions measure.

clue.text: More probing, rooting out name for willow

indicators.note: rooting out means digging up and removing, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: nosier means more inquisitive, more prying

explanation.surface: A nosy person digging around discovers a name for a willow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rooting out' takes N away from NOSIER; the surface makes it sound like digging up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a kind of willow whose pliant shoots are used in basketwork.

clue.text: Catch in piscine trap

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A fish is caught in a trap meant for fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch it, as a fisherman does.

clue.text: Cole Porter's song gets transposed all the time

indicators.note: transposed means swapped round, so the two halves of the song title change places

parts.note: Cole Porter wrote the song Night and Day; its last word is used here
the joining word of the Porter title Night and Day
the first word of the Porter title Night and Day, now moved to the end

explanation.surface: A Cole Porter standard is rearranged by a band and played constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter's song Night and Day has its two outer words swapped round, as signalled by 'gets transposed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means round the clock, continuously, which is what all the time means.

clue.text: Tawdry equipment's given to church

parts.note: kit means equipment; with the possessive 's it gives KIT'S

explanation.surface: Cheap gear has been donated to a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes showy, tasteless items, so it is a synonym of tawdry.

clue.text: Escape through sound and glide into anchorage

indicators.note: sound tells us a word is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: scarper is British slang for run away or escape
to flow is to glide along smoothly

explanation.surface: A ship escapes through a strait and drifts into harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a stretch of sea but signals that SCARPER is heard as SCAPA; Scapa Flow is the naval anchorage in Orkney.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa Flow in Orkney was the Royal Navy's great wartime anchorage.

clue.text: Whole range of colours as shown by artist in the forefront

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist
the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: An artist at the head of the group displays the full spectrum of colours.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW, the front of a vessel, is the forefront; 'in the forefront' is read as IN + BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow shows the whole spectrum, so it serves as a figure for a full range of colours.

clue.text: Secondary route over heath to institution

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a B road is a British secondary road
a moor is open heathland

explanation.surface: Directions to an asylum take a minor road across open heath.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadmoor is a high-security psychiatric hospital in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadmoor is a secure psychiatric institution in England.

clue.text: Shameless audacity shown by composer Heinrich without his son and father Henry

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Heinrich Schutz was a German baroque composer
S is the abbreviation for son
pa is father
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A composer's son and father show brazen nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without his son' removes S from SCHUTZ, leaving CHUTZ; the surface pretends the composer is family.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutzpah is a Yiddish loanword for brazen nerve or audacity.

clue.text: Hags who cooked tripe

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or falsified, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Old witches stirred up a dish of offal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' looks like what the hags cooked, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash and tripe are both slang for worthless nonsense.

clue.text: Chicken's loud cry, one of pain

parts.note: to yell is to give a loud cry
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A hen lets out a loud squawk because it is hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken's' is 'Chicken is': the adjective meaning cowardly, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang adjectives for cowardly.

clue.text: House with loan raised becomes a breeding-ground for problems

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a debt is a loan owed

explanation.surface: A mortgage on a house leads to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is a place where something, often undesirable, thrives and grows.

clue.text: This settles the argument — it's the most up-to date model

definitions.meaning: the final remark that ends a debate

definitions.text: it's the most up-to date model
definitions.meaning: the very latest design or fashion

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the decisive closing remark and the newest, most advanced version of something.

clue.text: More ancient tree

definitions.meaning: a small tree with white flowers and dark berries

explanation.definitionFit: Elder means older and is also the name of the tree that bears elderberries.

clue.text: Doctor's time taken up by nymph

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: taken up in a down clue means the word is reversed upwards

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A doctor's appointment is taken by a nymph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns DAY upwards into YAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Two musicians have rejected Arab's lute

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the oud is the lute of Arab music

explanation.surface: A pair of players turn down an Arab stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A duo is a pair of performers, here two musicians.

clue.text: Travel by bike-youth gets record going backwards

indicators.note: going backwards means the combined pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: a lad is a youth
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A cyclist boy gets hold of a disc that plays in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to work a bicycle's pedals, i.e. to travel by bike.

clue.text: Once my hob gets broken, it's full of holes

indicators.note: broken means smashed up, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: My cooking hob has cracked and now it is riddled with gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeycomb is a mass of wax cells, so it is something full of holes.

clue.text: Accompanying this letter, write movingly to husband after he comes first

indicators.note: comes first puts the word he at the very front
movingly means with motion, so the letters of write are shifted about

explanation.surface: A covering note tells someone to write tenderly to her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movingly' signals the anagram, and 'comes first' puts the pronoun at the front; the surface reads as a tender letter home.
explanation.definitionFit: Herewith is a formal word meaning with this letter or enclosed alongside.

clue.text: Loved making trouble with socialist

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
a red is a left-winger, a socialist

explanation.surface: Someone enjoyed stirring up trouble alongside a left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored is a past form meaning loved deeply.
